problem: Existing embodied benchmarks are short-horizon and procedural; none tests whether agents can accumulate multimodal evidence across multiple environments and make preference-aligned (explicit and implicit) decisions. Raw multimodal history fed in-context is noisy and expensive.
motivation: Agents are expected to act as decision-makers for users (e.g., apartment hunting), which needs long-horizon memory, comparison across candidates and inference of implicit preferences. Diagnosis shows that adding history helps up to a point (about 10 turns) and then degrades, so memory management, not context length, is a bottleneck.
key_idea: Compress long multimodal exploration history into a fixed small set of memory tokens with a preference-conditioned Perceiver-style compressor, injected as a soft prompt into a frozen VLM.
insight: Memory scaling is non-monotonic: more unfiltered history hurts, so selecting decision-relevant evidence matters more than context size. In the ablation, removing preference conditioning causes the largest drop (52.78 to 15.67), while removing visual memory (44.44) or hierarchical compression (41.67) costs less. Memory probing shows the tokens carry real evidence: zero and random memory give F1 of only 0.071 and 0.048, versus 0.719 for the full method.
method: Benchmark task: house-selection in ProcTHOR; N preferences in 7 categories, 1+3M candidate environments (1 golden, distractors in easy/medium/hard tiers); explicit and implicit tracks; default N=7, M=19; metrics Acc, nSAT, EE
Preference encoding: the frozen VLM turns requirements into keywords, whose text embeddings are pooled into one preference embedding
Step encoding: each step (ego image, map image, observation text, action text) is encoded and given step-id and environment-id embeddings

Preference-conditioned compression: learned queries Q0 plus a projection of the preference embedding cross-attend over each environment's steps, then self-attention; per-environment tokens are concatenated into global memory tokens
Memory injection: a trainable adapter maps the tokens into the frozen VLM embedding space as a soft-prompt prefix before the current prompt
Stage 1 training: a step-relevance classifier (positive/negative/unknown/irrelevant) with cross-entropy plus an attention-alignment loss
Stage 2 training: language-modeling loss on yes/no/unknown answers to memory QA, with the VLM frozen and gradients flowing to the adapter and compressor

setting.backbone: Qwen3VL-8B-Instruct (frozen) + trained Perceiver-style compressor and adapter; benchmark evaluation also uses Qwen3VL-30B-Thinking, Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, GPT-5.4
setting.training_data: Synthetic step-level relevance labels for stage 1 and preference-related memory QA (yes/no/unknown) for stage 2, from benchmark trajectories; scale not given in the text
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB image + map-view image + observation text + action text per step
setting.action_space: High-level exploration actions in ProcTHOR houses with up to 1500 steps (details in appendix)
setting.privileged: none stated; the training-time relevance labels come from ground-truth environment features

numbers.extra: About 3.8K memory tokens; 85.38% memory reduction vs the strongest baseline; +7.18 absolute Acc (15.74% relative) over the strongest baseline

numbers_note: The main-method comparison and ablations for the proposed method are given only in figures; the text gives 52.78 for the full method, 15.67 for -preference, 44.44 for -visual and 41.67 for -hierarchy. The memory probing F1 for the full method is 0.719. The benchmark is new, so no canonical benchmark name applies.
results: The best agent (GPT-5.4 with multimodal memory) reaches 58.3% accuracy against 83.3% for humans. The compressor on Qwen3VL-8B reaches 52.78% accuracy with about 3.8K tokens, versus about 60K for multimodal recent memory, and beats all memory baselines. It also reaches 83% on the web tasks against 72% for text-summary memory.
limitations: Evaluation is only on synthetic ProcTHOR houses with a small test set (accuracy values are multiples of about 5.6%, suggesting 18 instances per track), so statistical power is limited
The compressor needs step-level relevance supervision and was tested only with a frozen Qwen3VL-8B, and the strongest proprietary models were not paired with it
The main experimental results are shown mainly in figures, and the web-agent transfer covers only explicit requirements
